A 1-year-old male infant is brought to the emergency department by his foster mother, who reports that
he has been behaving unusually since this morning. His medical history is unremarkable. On
examination, the infant appears lethargic and has a distinct odor of alcohol and cigarettes. Multiple
bruises are noted on his shoulders, head, and buttocks. The left lower limb shows restricted range of
motion. Fundoscopic examination reveals bilateral retinal hemorrhages. His vital signs include a
temperature of 36.7°C (98°F), pulse of 121/min, respirations of 34/min, and blood pressure of 121/67
mmHg. Before the examination is completed, the foster mother expresses impatience and asks to
leave. When informed of the suspected diagnosis, she becomes angry and refuses treatment for the
child. What is the most appropriate immediate next step in management? Answer Choices: (A) Report
the mother to the police (B) Perform a skeletal survey to assess for additional injuries (C) Perform a
lumbar puncture to evaluate for meningitis (D) Administer intravenous antibiotics and fluids (E) Obtain
a court order for emergency medical treatment (F) Request an urgent CT scan and call neurosurgery
(G) Order a toxicology screen to evaluate for ingested substances (H) Obtain informed consent for
surgery (I) Protect the child from the mother (J) Contact child protective services
 A. Request an urgent CT scan and call neurosurgery
B. Protect the child from the mother
C. Administer intravenous antibiotics and fluids
D. Perform a lumbar puncture to evaluate for meningitis
E. Obtain a court order for emergency medical treatment
F. Obtain informed consent for surgery
G. Report the mother to the police
H. Contact child protective services
I. Perform a skeletal survey to assess for additional injuries
J. Order a toxicology screen to evaluate for ingested substances
